newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mitsubishi Motors Australia to raise output.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Motors Australia to raise output.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd (MMAL) said on Wednesday it would raise vehicle production at its Adelaide plant to 300 units a day in August, rising further to 310 units later in the year, from 280 units in June.
A Mitsubishi spokesman told Reuters the company expected to produce 61,500 units in 1997, up from 43,500 units in 1996.
MMAL managing director Mike Quinn said in a statement the move was necessary due to high demand for its Magna/Veruda range, both in Australia and overseas.

Quinn said earlier in the year the wholly-owned Mitsubishi Motors Corp subsidiary produced 260 units a day, progressively rising to 280 units but, with record sales - 38,720 units for the year to date compared to 29,500 at the same time in 1996 - had not been able to meet demand.

Mitsubishi expected in 1997 to export more than 18,000 vehicles to more than 20 countries which, along with exports of components, were forecast to result in export revenue of more than A$500 million, the statement said.
